items.title: test_ring_credential_loud.py misreports a missing `jq` as "the control is a no-op in BOTH states"

labels.name: status:untriaged

labels.name: self-improvement
labels.description: Agent-discovered out-of-scope work for the self-improvement triage lane

items.body:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent — misleading local failure mode in a gating self-test harness.

`scripts/tests/test_ring_credential_loud.py` extracts and EXECUTES the real `run:` script of `.github/workflows/fast-fix-ring.yml`'s `ring` job under bash with a stubbed `gh`. That script parses the stubbed `gh api` JSON with `jq` (`jq -r '.head_repo' <<<"$state"`, etc.).

On a box without `jq` on PATH, the command substitution yields an empty string, the head-repo guard takes the early-return branch (`resolved PR #123 head repo is not o/r (fork / cross-repo collision) — skipping.`) and the script exits 0 BEFORE ever reaching the `REGISTRY_RING_TOKEN` guard the suite exists to pin. Both credential-state tests then fail with assertions that accuse the production control of being broken:

- `AssertionError: ... exited 0 with REGISTRY_RING_TOKEN EMPTY — the ring was suppressed and the run still reported success. That is the #4966 defect`
- `AssertionError: ... did not dispatch jeswr/agent-account-registry even with the credential present — the control is a no-op in BOTH states, which is worse than the bug`

The control is fine; the harness dependency is missing. Installing `jq` turns the suite green immediately (verified: 9 tests OK). CI runners ship `jq`, so this is local-only — but it points a developer at a non-existent high-severity regression in exactly the lane whose whole purpose is to stop a silent no-op control from looking healthy.

Suggested fix: have `_Harness` assert `shutil.which("jq")` (or `unittest.skipUnless`) up front, so an absent interpreter dependency reports as a harness precondition rather than as a false accusation against the guard.

> 🤖 Discovered by the SPARQ worker while implementing #3176. Out-of-scope for that PR; captured as follow-up.
<!-- sparq-followup:v1 -->

items.body:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent — found while reproducing the full gate locally for PR #5682.

**What.** `scripts/tests/test_ring_credential_loud.py` extracts the real `run:` script from `fast-fix-ring.yml` / `batch-merge.yml` and executes it under bash with a stubbed `gh` on PATH. Those scripts also shell out to **`jq`** (e.g. `fast-fix-ring.yml` `jq -r '.head_repo' <<<"$state"`). The harness stubs `gh` but not `jq`, and does not check that `jq` exists.

**Why it matters.** On a box without `jq` the extracted script takes the fork/cross-repo skip branch (`resolved PR #123 head repo is not o/r (fork / cross-repo collision) — skipping.`) and the suite fails with two assertions that read as real product defects:

- `fast-fix-ring.yml:ring did not dispatch jeswr/agent-account-registry even with the credential present — the control is a no-op in BOTH states, which is worse than the bug`
- `fast-fix-ring.yml:ring exited 0 with REGISTRY_RING_TOKEN EMPTY — ... That is the #4966 defect: ~130 rings vanished into green runs.`

Both are false here: installing `jq` turns the suite green with no source change. An agent debugging locally is pointed straight at a #4966 regression that does not exist. This is the opposite of the good behaviour its sibling already has — `scripts/tests/test_typos_allowlist.sh` fails fast and unambiguously with `FATAL: 'typos' binary not on PATH`.

**Suggested fix.** In `_Harness` (or `setUpClass`), assert the external binaries the extracted scripts depend on are present — `shutil.which("jq")` — and fail (or skip) with an explicit `jq not on PATH` message, mirroring the typos self-test. Same audit for any other unstubbed binary the two ring scripts call.

**Out of scope for #5682**, which only edits `pull_request:` `types:` triggers + docs; `fast-fix-ring.yml` and this test are untouched by that diff.

> 🤖 Discovered by the SPARQ worker while implementing #5215. Out-of-scope for that PR; captured as follow-up.
<!-- sparq-followup:v1 -->

labels.name: self-improvement

items.body:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent — found while reproducing the full docs-quality gate locally for PR #5177.

`scripts/tests/test_ring_credential_loud.py` drives the real `fast-fix-ring.yml:ring` step body through bash. That step parses its state JSON with `jq` (`jq -r '.head_repo' <<<"$state"`, `jq -e --arg l ...`). The test harness stubs `gh`, but nothing asserts `jq` is present.

When `jq` is missing, every `jq` call yields the empty string, so the step takes the `head repo is not o/r (fork / cross-repo collision) — skipping` branch and exits 0. Two tests then fail with actively misleading messages:

- `test_present_credential_rings_and_exits_zero`: "did not dispatch ... even with the credential present — the control is a no-op in BOTH states, which is worse than the bug"
- `test_empty_credential_exits_non_zero_and_annotates`: "exited 0 with REGISTRY_RING_TOKEN EMPTY ... That is the #4966 defect: ~130 rings vanished into green runs"

Both messages accuse the production ring of the exact regression the file exists to prevent, when the real cause is a missing local tool. Verified: installing `jq` 1.7.1 turns the suite green with no source change.

This costs review/worker time because the failure looks like a genuine, severe CI defect. Suggested fix: add a `shutil.which('jq')` precondition that either `skipUnless`-skips or fails with an explicit "jq is required to exercise the ring step body" message — the same tool-dependency guard the other bash-driving suites in `scripts/tests/` would benefit from. CI is unaffected (ubuntu-latest ships jq), so this is purely local-reproduction robustness.

> 🤖 Discovered by the SPARQ worker while implementing #2892. Out-of-scope for that PR; captured as follow-up.
<!-- sparq-followup:v1 -->

labels.name: status:untriaged

labels.name: self-improvement

items.body:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

`scripts/tests/test_ring_credential_loud.py` extracts the `ring` step's `run:` script from `.github/workflows/fast-fix-ring.yml` and executes it against a stubbed `gh`. That script parses the PR state with `jq -r '.head_repo'`. When `jq` is NOT on PATH, the command substitution yields the empty string, so the ring script takes its `head repo is not o/r (fork / cross-repo collision) — skipping` branch and exits 0 **before** ever reaching the empty-credential check.

The test then fails with a misleading diagnosis:

```
AssertionError: 0 == 0 : fast-fix-ring.yml:ring exited 0 with REGISTRY_RING_TOKEN EMPTY — the ring was
suppressed and the run still reported success. That is the #4966 defect: ~130 rings vanished into green runs.
```

i.e. it blames the #4966 regression it guards, when the real cause is a missing ambient tool. Installing `jq` turns the whole file green (9/9), so there is no repo defect — only a bad failure message.

The harness docstring calls itself hermetic ("Executes an extracted `run:` script with a stubbed `gh` on PATH"), but `jq` is an undeclared ambient dependency. GitHub-hosted runners preinstall `jq` so CI never sees this; it only bites local reproduction, where it costs real investigation time and points the reader at the wrong subsystem.

Suggested fix: add a `shutil.which("jq")` precondition to `_Harness.__init__` (or a module-level `skipUnless`) that fails/skips with an explicit "jq is required by the extracted ring script" message, so a missing dependency can never masquerade as the #4966 defect.

Found while reproducing the full CI matrix locally for PR #5049 (docs-only diff); out of scope for that PR.

items.title: fast-fix-ring and batch-merge's ring job have never sent a ring: REGISTRY_RING_TOKEN does not exist, and both fail soft to a green run (~2000 runs, 0 effect)
items.body:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

`fast-fix-ring` and `batch-merge`'s `ring` job both end in a single privileged call gated on `secrets.REGISTRY_RING_TOKEN`. **That secret does not exist**, so both controls resolve it to the empty string, take the fail-soft branch, and emit a `::notice::` nobody reads. Across ~2000 runs neither has ever performed its one mutation.

## The secret is absent — measured at runtime, not inferred from config

`repos/sparq-org/sparq/actions/secrets` contains exactly:

```
OPENALEX_API_KEY, ORCHESTRATOR_APP_ID, ORCHESTRATOR_APP_PRIVATE_KEY
```

I could not read org-level secrets (`orgs/sparq-org/actions/secrets` → 403), so repo-level absence alone would not settle whether an org secret is inherited. The runtime environment dump settles it. From run `30411348407`, job `fast-fix ring (advisory)` — and these are runtime log lines, not echoed script source (that log contains **zero** `ESC[36;1m`-prefixed lines):

```
GH_TOKEN: ***
REGISTRY_RING_TOKEN:
REPO: sparq-org/sparq
HEAD_SHA: 72ef1b57c074abb75dcffc45f16dfec224c46252
```

`GH_TOKEN` renders as `***` because a secret with a value is masked. `REGISTRY_RING_TOKEN` renders as **nothing at all** — it has no value, at repo or org level.

The guard it feeds, `.github/workflows/fast-fix-ring.yml:212`:

```bash
if [ -z "${REGISTRY_RING_TOKEN}" ]; then
```

## Blast radius

| control | runs | executed past `if:` | rings sent |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fast-fix-ring` | **1969** (1614 skipped, 355 executed) | 32 sampled, **12** passed every eligibility check | **0** |
| `batch-merge` `ring` job | 12/12 sampled push runs | all reached the guard | **0** |

Extrapolating the sampled rate, roughly **130 rings** have been suppressed. The cross-repo doorbell is these workflows' *only* write capability — `fast-fix-ring.yml:94` calls it "The one WRITE capability" — so with it empty the entire control is a no-op wrapped around an eligibility computation whose result is discarded.

**Verdict: INERT** for both, and INERT since inception rather than by regression.

## Why it stayed invisible

The guard is deliberately fail-soft: a missing token produces a `::notice::` and a **green** run. That is a defensible choice for an advisory lane, but it means the difference between "the ring fired" and "the ring cannot fire, and never could" is not visible in any field a monitor queries. 1969 green runs, zero effect.

This is the same shape as the "signal exists, nothing consumes it" class: the control correctly detects that it is disabled and then reports that fact into a void.

## Suggested fix

Decide which of these two is true and make the code say so:

1. **The ring is wanted** — provision `REGISTRY_RING_TOKEN` (or switch to the `ORCHESTRATOR_APP_*` App credentials already present in this repo, which would avoid a long-lived cross-repo PAT and address the exfiltration concern the workflow header raises at `:5-19` re #3474).
2. **The ring is not wanted** — delete both jobs rather than run ~2000 no-op invocations that read as healthy.

Either way, the fail-soft branch should be loud enough to be noticed on its *first* occurrence — a rolling issue, or a red advisory run — rather than a `::notice::`. A control that is disabled by missing configuration and silent about it is indistinguishable from one that is working.

Related: `.github/workflows/pr-backlog.yml:96` carries `EXCLUDE_PR: "2431"` for a PR that merged 2026-07-17 — dead config in the same family, trivial to clear.

Found during a survey of whether each orchestration control has ever actually *acted*, as distinct from having *run*.

items.title: SECURITY: REGISTRY_RING_TOKEN exposed to PR-authored workflow code (ci-summary fix-ring on pull_request)
items.body:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

**Severity: HIGH.** The fast-fix ring job in .github/workflows/ci-summary.yml runs on pull_request and reads secrets.REGISTRY_RING_TOKEN. For pull_request events GitHub takes the workflow definition from the PR head, and same-repo PRs (our sparq-agent/* agent branches) receive repository secrets — so a malicious/compromised agent PR editing ci-summary.yml could exfiltrate the cross-repo ring token.

Latent: REGISTRY_RING_TOKEN is not configured yet, so the job currently fail-softs — but the hole must close before the secret is added.

Merged unreviewed via #3430 (verdict-extractor substring-matched the quoted instruction and false-passed a needs-changes verdict; extractor now line-anchored).

Fix: move the ring to a separate workflow_run-triggered workflow (on: workflow_run: workflows: [ci-summary], types: [completed]; guard conclusion==failure && event==pull_request). workflow_run always uses the base-branch definition, isolated from PR head content. Keep the live-state checks + fail-soft; remove the fix-ring job from ci-summary.yml.
